extracted.intended_audience: cartoonists and entrants to the CIPE Global Editorial Cartoon Competition (students, professional, and amateur cartoonists worldwide)
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting editorial cartoons to the CIPE Global Editorial Cartoon Competition according to the contest's eligibility, file-format, judging, and rights requirements. Covers digital and hard-copy technical specs, entry limits, and judging/publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Enter / Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry is open to participants of all ages, including students, professional, and amateur cartoonists. Entrants may hold citizenship in or live in any country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest is international and open to all ages and skill levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission limits per entrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants may submit a maximum of two cartoons in each of three categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the per-category maximum of two cartoons; exceeding may lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred format: .jpg (.png and .tiff files are also acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit in .jpg when possible; .png and .tiff are acceptable alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital image technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital versions: Minimum resolution of 300 dpi and dimensions of 600 pixels wide and 400 pixels high (must be suitable for printing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files must meet minimum dpi and pixel dimensions to be suitable for printing; low-resolution submissions risk rejection or poor reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard-copy size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard-copy versions: A4 (210 X 297 mm) or A3 (297 X 410 mm) and Letter (216 × 279 mm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting physical copies, adhere to these paper sizes for handling and scanning/printing consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed cartoon formats and sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may include different sizes of cartoons – single panel, a strip, or a two-tier strip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various panel formats are permitted; ensure clarity and legibility across the allowed formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static image requirement (no animation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be static images with no Flash or other animation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animated formats or interactive content are not permitted and will be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: English translations MUST be provided for any text or captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide English translations for all non-English text to ensure judges and the public can understand the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming / metadata requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions (files) MUST have the name and country of entrant included in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include entrant name and country in the filename or the submitted file itself; failure to follow entry directions may result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and intellectual property compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be the original work of the contestant, must not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, rights of privacy, or other intellectual property or other rights of any person or entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you own or have the rights to all elements of the cartoon; do not use copyrighted material without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria for finalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries awarded 'finalist' status will be judged according to the judges’ determination of creativity, cleverness, draftsmanship, relevance to the category to which the cartoon was submitted, courage, and humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalist selection emphasizes originality, technical skill, thematic fit, boldness, and comedic impact as determined by the judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet voting for Finalist Category winners
rubrics_metrics.description: In Internet voting to determine Finalist Category winners, the top scoring Entry will be declared the Contest Category Winner ('Winner').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public/internet voting selects the category winner among finalists; ensure work can appeal in online voting if eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-break and judges' discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: In event of a tie, Winner will be determined based on the judges’ discretion. Judges’ decisions are final and binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with voting, judges retain final authority in ties and overall decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-manipulation and disqualification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is evidence of internet voting manipulation by the entrant or by outside parties, category winners may be disqualified based on the judges’ discretion. Sponsor reserves the right to disqualify any Entry for any reason, in its sole and absolute discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to manipulate voting; such behavior risks disqualification. The sponsor may also disqualify for other reasons as they deem appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and rule-violation consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of plagiarism or any violation of competition rules will result in the disqualification from this and any future CIPE Global Editorial Cartoon Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism or rule breaches carry severe penalties including exclusion from future contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize amount and payment method
rubrics_metrics.description: First Place Category winners in each category will receive $1,000.00 USD, provided by New Generation Foundation. Prizes will be provided by electronic funds transfer or other means if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners should expect electronic payment and may need to provide banking information to receive awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner banking information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To accommodate electronic funds transfer, Winners will be required to furnish banking information to receive awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide accurate banking details if you win; failure to provide may affect prize delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication rights and sharing permission
rubrics_metrics.description: By participating in this competition entrants allow CIPE and New Generation Foundation the right to publish contest submissions online, in print, or in other media, and to allow other organizations with similar missions to publish cartoon works submitted to the contest. CIPE and New Generation Foundation will provide proper credit to the cartoonists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants grant publication rights to CIPE/NGF and affiliated organizations; expect your work to be republished with credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By participating in this competition, entrants agree to fully indemnify and hold harmless CIPE and New Generation Foundation for any action or result that may arise from form their role in producing and sponsoring this competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants assume legal responsibility for issues arising from their submission and must indemnify the organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Any views expressed or intimated by the cartoonist are his or her own and do not necessarily represent the views of the Center for International Private Enterprise (CIPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers disavow endorsement of submitted cartoon viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence for fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Due diligence will be conducted throughout the competition process to ensure fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers will perform checks and oversight to promote a fair contest.
